memory_update.text: WEST is the primary reference candidate for the B2B coffee/tea/extract/RTD beverage supply node because its public filings directly map to restaurant, foodservice, c-store, hospitality, CPG, and non-commercial channels, and Conway is a major capacity asset to track.

THS should be tracked as an embedded private-label coffee capacity owner after acquiring Farmer Brothers' Northlake facility and direct-ship coffee business; exposure is real but may be diluted inside broader private-label packaged foods.

FARM is a high-risk micro-cap exception with unusually direct DSD foodservice coffee/tea/equipment-service exposure; later layers must test liquidity, leverage, route economics, and sustained profitability before promotion.

JVA is a speculative shadow candidate for wholesale green coffee and private-label foodservice supply; direct relevance exists, but micro-cap liquidity and commodity exposure make it unsuitable for strong conclusions without further filing review.

The most investable chokepoint signals for this node are not consumer coffee brands, but integrated sourcing, extract/RTD manufacturing capacity, private-label roasting, direct-store-delivery reliability, equipment service, and traceability/sustainability programs.

Need a follow-up search for equipment vendors, syrup/flavor suppliers, tea suppliers, water-filtration/dispense systems, beverage QA/testing, and route-density software because this pass mainly surfaced coffee/extract manufacturing names.

node: B2B coffee roasting, extracts, tea, syrups, and beverage ingredient supply
summary: Expanded the US-listed universe for B2B coffee and beverage ingredient supply with a two-lane funnel. The reference lane is Westrock Coffee as the most direct public pure-play scale supplier for coffee, tea, extracts, RTD and foodservice channels. The underfollowed lane includes TreeHouse Foods as a private-label coffee capacity owner, Farmer Bros. as a micro-cap DSD coffee/tea/equipment-service supplier to foodservice accounts, and Coffee Holding Co. as a speculative micro-cap wholesale/private-label coffee supplier. This node appears investable but fragile: the strongest chokepoint evidence is capacity, traceability, customer customization, and direct-store reliability; the main risks are commodity coffee volatility, leverage, customer concentration, and weak profitability.
